about: Definitions only. Measured values live in each run's tpm.json; baselines live in tpm_baseline.json. threshold_status: TBD (no limit yet), TBR (proposed limit, shown with margin, never pass or fail), Confirmed (a limit that fails a run when breached). A threshold is in the TPM's unit, or {factor, of} for a limit relative to a run fact (exposure_seconds, frame_interval_seconds). cold_only: true marks a limit that applies only to a --cold run (the file cache was dropped before it); a warm run still measures the value but gets no limit for it.

tpms.name: time_to_app_ready
tpms.title: Time until the app is ready
tpms.why: You start the app and want to use it before you lose your train of thought.
tpms.method: performance mark in the page
tpms.source: Nielsen response-time limits (0.1 s feels instant, 1 s keeps the flow of thought, 10 s is the attention limit); 5 s threshold, 2 s objective is reachable on this CPU (measured about 1.8 s).

tpms.name: time_to_app_ready_cold
tpms.title: Time until the app is ready, cold start
tpms.why: The first start after a reboot reads everything from the disk, and you still want to begin without losing your train of thought.
tpms.method: performance mark in the page, first load of the run; the limit applies only to a --cold run (files dropped from the page cache before the run)
tpms.source: proposal 2026-11-06

tpms.name: first_display_open[{display}]
tpms.title: First open of a display, cold start
tpms.why: The first time you open a display after a cold start, the click should still answer quickly.
tpms.method: click-to-settled time of the first visit to each display in lap 1 of the flow; the limit applies only to a --cold run
tpms.source: proposal 2026-11-06

tpms.name: first_rpc[{rpc}]
tpms.title: First backend call, cold start
tpms.why: The first query on real data reads database pages that are not in memory yet.
tpms.method: latency of the first call of each method in the run (the page's own timing of the fetch); the limit applies only to a --cold run
tpms.source: proposal 2026-11-06

tpms.name: display_switch_median

tpms.method: click-to-settled timing in the flow

tpms.name: catalog_failures

tpms.source: No limit set yet. The user sets it. Added 2026-11-06 after a sandboxed bright-star driver returned no stars.

tpms.name: disk_read_mb[{process_group}]
tpms.title: Disk read per process group
tpms.why: How much the app makes the disk read, group by group (backend, pool workers, INDI, Siril, GraXpert, denoise tools, Electron, browser).
tpms.method: Resource sampler (resource_usage.py): reads /proc/<pid>/io, stat and status of the backend and every process under it once a second. Sum of read_bytes (bytes the process caused to be read from storage) over every process of the group, last sample minus first. A process that ends between two samples keeps its last seen value, so the number is a lower bound for very short programs. rchar and wchar (bytes passed to read and write calls, file cache included) are kept in info.resources for information.
tpms.source: No limit set yet. Needs a baseline run and a user need first.

tpms.name: disk_write_mb[{process_group}]
tpms.title: Disk written per process group
tpms.why: How much the app makes the disk write, group by group; it shows what hurts a drive or a slow network share.
tpms.method: Resource sampler (resource_usage.py): reads /proc/<pid>/io, stat and status of the backend and every process under it once a second. Sum of write_bytes over every process of the group, last sample minus first. Lower bound for very short programs.
tpms.source: No limit set yet. Needs a baseline run and a user need first.

tpms.name: disk_read_mb_per_lap[{process_group}]
tpms.title: Disk read per lap
tpms.why: How much the disk reads while the flow visits every display once.
tpms.method: Resource sampler (resource_usage.py): reads /proc/<pid>/io, stat and status of the backend and every process under it once a second. The read_bytes of the group in the wall-clock window of one lap of the flow (flow-metrics.json lapWindows), median over the laps. Only runs with the display flow.
tpms.source: No limit set yet. Needs a baseline run and a user need first.

tpms.name: disk_write_mb_per_lap[{process_group}]
tpms.title: Disk written per lap
tpms.why: How much the disk writes while the flow visits every display once.
tpms.method: Resource sampler (resource_usage.py): reads /proc/<pid>/io, stat and status of the backend and every process under it once a second. The write_bytes of the group in the window of one lap, median over the laps. Only runs with the display flow.
tpms.source: No limit set yet. Needs a baseline run and a user need first.

tpms.name: backend_tree_cpu_time
tpms.title: Backend process tree CPU time
tpms.why: The backend starts many programs; its own CPU time alone hides most of the cost of a stack or an analysis.
tpms.method: Resource sampler. Sum over the live processes of the backend's tree of their own CPU time plus the CPU time of their finished, collected children (the kernel's cutime and cstime, so a child that ends between samples is still counted); last sample minus first.
tpms.source: No limit set yet. Needs a baseline run and a user need first.

tpms.name: backend_tree_peak_rss
tpms.title: Backend process tree peak memory
tpms.why: The backend plus Siril, GraXpert and the pool workers share the computer's memory with KStars and the browser; only the sum shows an out-of-memory risk.
tpms.method: Resource sampler. The largest sum of resident memory over all processes of the backend's tree in any one sample (once a second). A peak shorter than a second can be missed; info.resources.trees.backend.peak_sum_mb is the sum of every process's own peak (an upper bound).
tpms.source: No limit set yet. Needs a baseline run and a user need first.

tpms.name: nvidia_util_percent_mean
tpms.title: NVIDIA utilization, mean
tpms.why: How busy the NVIDIA card is during the run; GraXpert and the denoise tools run on it.
tpms.method: nvidia-smi utilization.gpu every 2 seconds (setup_fingerprint.py nvidia-sample), mean over the run. Empty when there is no NVIDIA card. Reading nvidia-smi can keep the card awake.
tpms.source: No limit set yet. Needs a baseline run and a user need first.

tpms.name: nvidia_util_percent_peak
tpms.title: NVIDIA utilization, peak
tpms.why: The busiest moment of the NVIDIA card.
tpms.method: Same samples, largest value.
tpms.source: No limit set yet. Needs a baseline run and a user need first.

tpms.name: nvidia_memory_mb_peak
tpms.title: NVIDIA memory in use, peak
tpms.why: GPU memory the run needs, to check that the card's memory is enough. The value is what the whole card has in use (the desktop included), not only the run.
tpms.method: nvidia-smi memory.used every 2 seconds, largest value.
tpms.source: No limit set yet. Needs a baseline run and a user need first.

tpms.name: processing_stage_seconds[{stage}]
tpms.title: Stacking stage wall time
tpms.why: Where the minutes of a stack go; a change that slows one stage shows here before it shows in the total.
tpms.method: processing_run.py: the Image Processing display's own RPC calls (processing:stack, then the analysis steps), polled until the job ends. The stack job logs one line 'Stage N of M' at the start of each stage, with a time to the millisecond (processing:job_log_tail). A stage runs to the next stage's line; the last one to the end of the job. A skipped stage gives no TPM.
tpms.source: No limit set yet. Needs a baseline run and a user need first.

tpms.name: processing_stage_cpu_seconds[{stage}]
tpms.title: Stacking stage CPU time
tpms.why: CPU the backend and its programs use in a stage (Siril's threads count).
tpms.method: processing_run.py: the Image Processing display's own RPC calls (processing:stack, then the analysis steps), polled until the job ends. CPU time of the backend's process tree inside the stage window, from the 0.5 s samples (resource_usage.py).
tpms.source: No limit set yet. Needs a baseline run and a user need first.

tpms.name: processing_stage_peak_rss_mb[{stage}]
tpms.title: Stacking stage peak memory
tpms.why: The memory a stage needs, backend and programs together.
tpms.method: processing_run.py: the Image Processing display's own RPC calls (processing:stack, then the analysis steps), polled until the job ends. Largest sum of resident memory of the backend's process tree in the stage window (samples every 0.5 s, plus the sample before and after).
tpms.source: No limit set yet. Needs a baseline run and a user need first.

tpms.name: processing_stage_disk_read_mb[{stage}]
tpms.title: Stacking stage disk read
tpms.why: How much a stage reads from storage (frames, calibration frames, catalogs).
tpms.method: processing_run.py: the Image Processing display's own RPC calls (processing:stack, then the analysis steps), polled until the job ends. read_bytes of every process of the backend's tree in the stage window.
tpms.source: No limit set yet. Needs a baseline run and a user need first.

tpms.name: processing_stage_disk_write_mb[{stage}]
tpms.title: Stacking stage disk written

tpms.method: processing_run.py: the Image Processing display's own RPC calls (processing:stack, then the analysis steps), polled until the job ends. write_bytes of every process of the backend's tree in the stage window.

tpms.name: processing_stage_nvidia_util_percent_mean[{stage}]

tpms.method: processing_run.py: the Image Processing display's own RPC calls (processing:stack, then the analysis steps), polled until the job ends. Mean of the nvidia-smi utilization rows (every 2 seconds) inside the stage window. Empty for a stage shorter than the sampling interval, or with no NVIDIA card.

tpms.name: processing_total_seconds
tpms.title: Stack and analysis wall time
tpms.why: How long the user waits from pressing Process to the end of the analysis for one target.
tpms.method: processing_run.py: the Image Processing display's own RPC calls (processing:stack, then the analysis steps), polled until the job ends. Stack job time (from the RPC call to the job's completion time) plus the time of every analysis step.
tpms.source: No limit set yet. Needs a baseline run and a user need first.

tpms.name: processing_frame_count
tpms.title: Frames in the stack input
tpms.why: The input size of the run, so two runs can be told to have the same input. Fixed by the target and the camera.
tpms.method: processing_run.py: the Image Processing display's own RPC calls (processing:stack, then the analysis steps), polled until the job ends. Frames of the chosen camera in target:get_files (spectroscopy frames left out), as sent to processing:stack. The hash of their paths is in info.processing.plan.paths_sha.
tpms.source: No limit set yet. Needs a baseline run and a user need first.

tpms.name: processing_failed_jobs
tpms.title: Failed processing jobs
tpms.why: A stack or analysis job that fails or times out makes every other number of the run meaningless.
tpms.method: processing_run.py: the Image Processing display's own RPC calls (processing:stack, then the analysis steps), polled until the job ends. The stack job counts if it did not complete; each analysis step counts if a job it started failed, was cancelled or timed out.
tpms.source: No limit set yet. Needs a baseline run and a user need first.

tpms.name: analysis_seconds[{step}]
tpms.title: Analysis step wall time
tpms.why: How long each analysis the display offers takes after the stack: photometry (Analyze Target), frame measurements and the stack comparison.
tpms.method: processing_run.py: the Image Processing display's own RPC calls (processing:stack, then the analysis steps), polled until the job ends. From the RPC call until every job it started has ended (processing:list_jobs for the target, new jobs only; the quality calls do not return their job's number).
tpms.source: No limit set yet. Needs a baseline run and a user need first.
